argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Reductio ad absurdum and internal critique
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate - premises are often embedded in examples and dialectical moves

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High - engages with objections and responses
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High - all moves directly support the thesis
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate - relies on contested interpretations of James

distinctions_drawn: Tolerance as a standard vs. tolerance as a value
explicit_definitions_given: Demand: a moral claim that prescribes action
Standard of tolerance: a criterion that demands must accommodate other demands

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Considers and refutes a tolerance-based response
objections_raised: Conflicting demands cannot be arbitrated if all are equal
Tolerance standard contradicts James's rejection of common essence
James's own demands are intolerant (e.g., against moral realism and other theories)

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, thought experiments, textual interpretation

philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Moral pluralism, tolerance, coherence of pragmatist ethics

summary_of_core_decisions: The essay argues that James's moral theory is incoherent because (1) treating all demands as equally good leads to unresolvable conflicts, and (2) any attempt to introduce a standard of tolerance fails because James's own demands are intolerant. The argument proceeds by internal critique, showing that James's theory cannot meet its own standards.
